name: Traefik
description: Reverse proxy that routes incoming traffic to your containers and manages their TLS certificates.
about: Routes traffic using labels on your application containers and can request Let's Encrypt certificates. Set hostname or path rules with traefik.http.routers labels. Traefik and the target containers must share a network.

variables.label: Data folder
variables.description: Holds acme.json, where Traefik keeps the ACME account and the certificates it was issued. Traefik creates the file with 0600 permissions and refuses one restored from a backup with looser ones.

variables.label: Runtime socket
variables.description: Traefik reads containers and their labels through this socket, mounted read-only. Podman's is usually /run/podman/podman.sock.

variables.label: HTTP port
variables.description: Host port for the web entryPoint, which listens on :80 inside the container. An HTTP-01 challenge only succeeds when port 80 from the internet lands here.

variables.label: HTTPS port
variables.description: Host port for the websecure entryPoint, which listens on :443 inside the container. A TLS-ALPN-01 challenge only succeeds when port 443 from the internet lands here.

variables.label: Route to every container
variables.description: Routes containers by default unless they have traefik.enable=false. When off, each routed container needs traefik.enable=true.

variables.label: Let's Encrypt email
variables.description: Turns on automatic certificates for every router on the websecure entryPoint. Leave blank to run without them.

variables.label: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
variables.description: Answers every request on the HTTP port with a permanent redirect to the HTTPS one. Turn it on once certificates are working.

variables.label: Publish the dashboard
variables.description: Publishes the dashboard and read-only API on port 8080 without authentication, exposing routing configuration to anyone who can reach it.

variables.label: Routing config folder
variables.description: Mounted read-only at /etc/traefik/dynamic and watched for changes. Drop .yml, .yaml, or .toml files here to route to hosts outside the runtime, or to define middlewares. An empty folder is fine.

variables.label: Certificate challenge
variables.description: How Let's Encrypt checks that you control the domain. Either way, that port has to reach this host from the internet. Ignored while the email is blank.

variables.label: Let's Encrypt server
variables.description: Staging issues untrusted certificates against far higher rate limits. Use it while you are getting the setup right.

variables.label: Log level
variables.description: Blank leaves Traefik at ERROR, so a working proxy prints almost nothing. Raise it when a route is not showing up.

variables.label: Access log
variables.description: Writes one line per proxied request to the container log, in the common log format.

variables.label: Timezone
variables.description: IANA name used for timestamps in Traefik's log output.
